newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sells indebted cannery, plastic maker.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sells indebted cannery, plastic maker.

text.p: Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said on Monday it has sold an indebted cannery factory and a debt-ridden plastic maker, initially slated for liquidation, for a total of 11 million levs to two buyers.
Seventy percent of the indebted Gotse Delchev-based Pirinplast plant was sold to one of its creditors, Bulgarleasing joint stock company, for 1.0 million levs, the agency said in a statement.

Under the deal Bulgarleasing pledged to remit some 9.8 million German marks of the debt owed to it by Pirinplast on the date of the signing of the contract and to reschedule the rest of Pirinplast's debt to it over five years.
Bulgarleasing also has to invest 35 million levs in the plant over the next five years.
The plant produces plastic materials for industrial and domestic use and exports some 30 percent of its output.
Its turnover for last year amounted to 185 million levs.
Pirinplast was initially on a government list of state loss-making firms slated for closure under the government's structural reform programme.

Sixty percent of Vitamina cannery was sold to Bulgarian-Greek joint venture TKM Fruit and Juices Manufacturing Ltd for 10.0 million levs, payable in cash on the day of the signing of the contract, the agency said.
The Sofia-registered buyer also pledged to settle 1.7 billion levs worth of outstanding debt of Vitamina to creditor banks and to invest some 161 million levs in it over five years.
The Stamboliisky-based plant produces fruit and vegetable juices and canned food. Some 67 percent of its output are earmarked for export.
Its turnover for last year totalled 318.3 million levs ($4.7 million).
The Privatisation Agency also said it sold the Yavor-Akatsia hotel in the Black Sea resort of Slanchev Bryag for 28 million levs payable on the day of the signing of the contract.
Under the deal the buyer, Nessebar Inn Ltd also has to invest some 35 million levs in the hotel over five years. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
